msg: (A) the susceptance null IS the best setting, demonstrated at the REAL operating point (R = 50, 5.4 pF, 19.5 nH): RL at the null minus RL at 0.90x the null total C = 5.640 dB. The pre-re-route bench had to run this test at a fictitious 30 nH because the as-routed board needed negative trimmer values; it does not any more.
(A) same test 10% ABOVE the null: 5.640 dB. Symmetric with dopt_m10, which is what a true minimum of |Gamma| looks like.
(A) 0.80x the null total C costs 10.666 dB.
(A) 1.25x the null total C costs 12.468 dB.
(A) the trimmer setting the scaling test is centred on is the board's own: 2.3708 pF of a delivered 1-30 pF part.

(A) THE REASON THIS TEST IS NOW LEGITIMATE: the 0.80x point needs 0.8167 pF of trimmer. That is below the 1 pF stop by 0.18 pF, so the -20% arm is a hair outside the orderable range while the -10% arm (1.5938 pF) is comfortably inside; asserted as a min so a bench that silently went back to negative capacitor values fails. The pre-re-route board needed -2.5 pF here.
(A) the +25% arm needs 4.3135 pF - inside the part.

(B) README NUMBER, new low edge: the smallest residual series L the delivered Johanson 5602 can null EXACTLY at the nominal 5.4 pF port is 16.041 nH. The pre-re-route README quoted 14.279 nH against a 4.7 pF port; that value is now outside this window, so a reverted parasitic trips here.
(B) README NUMBER, new high edge: 96.661 nH. The pre-re-route figure was 94.376 nH; a 35 pF trimmer (no such part) against the same 5.4 pF port would say 113.6 nH.

(B) README NUMBER, achievable adjustment range: 80.62 nH wide (16.04 to 96.66 nH). The width is nearly parasitic-independent (80.10 / 80.62 / 81.17 / 81.50 nH across 4.7 / 5.4 / 6.1 / 6.5 pF); it is the POSITION that moves.
(B) the low endpoint as series reactance at 25.0 MHz: 2.520 ohm.

(B) the high endpoint as series reactance: 15.183 ohm. Still BELOW the 16.242 ohm point where Reff alone breaks 26 dB at R = 50 (reff_limit.cir xcap_r50_ohm), so at nominal resistance the trimmer's top stop, not the resistance transformation, is what ends the exact-null range.
(B) ENVELOPE across the port-parasitic band, low edge at 4.7 pF: 14.279 nH.
(B) ENVELOPE, high edge at 4.7 pF: 94.376 nH.
(B) ENVELOPE across the port-parasitic band, low edge at 6.1 pF: 17.806 nH.
(B) ENVELOPE, high edge at 6.1 pF: 98.976 nH.
(B) ENVELOPE across the port-parasitic band, low edge at 6.5 pF: 18.816 nH.
(B) ENVELOPE, high edge at 6.5 pF: 100.312 nH.
(B) the window also moves with RESISTANCE: at R = 49 the low edge is 15.404 nH.

(B) and at R = 52.5 it is 17.689 nH - the highest low edge over the select-on-test range plus the +5% corner, and therefore the number the board's residual has to clear to be two-sided everywhere. 18.5 nH clears it by 0.81 nH.
(B) high edge at R = 52.5: 107.703 nH.
(B) DELIVERED PART, low end: 5.4 pF port + 1 pF at full CCW = 6.40 pF total shunt.
(B) DELIVERED PART, high end: 5.4 + 30 = 35.40 pF. A 1-35 pF part - which is on no BOM - would read 40.40 pF.
(B) simulated proof, not just algebra: at L = lnull_lo with the trimmer pinned at its 1 pF stop the null is REAL, not a clamped mistune - 57.94 dB, whose entire residual is Reff = 50.127 ohm.
(B) same at the top: L = lnull_hi with the trimmer at its 30 pF stop gives 27.12 dB. The whole 16.04-96.66 nH window is spec-legal at nominal resistance, by 1.1 dB at its worst end.
(B) same check at the 6.5 pF end of the parasitic band: 55.17 dB.

(B) the tightest corner of the window analysis: top of the window at the 6.5 pF parasitic, 26.50 dB - above crit. 2 by only 0.5 dB. A build whose residual is near 100 nH is spec-legal and has no margin. The board is at 19.5.
(B) 4.7 pF low edge: 59.96 dB.
(B) 4.7 pF high edge: 27.51 dB.

(C) THE HEADLINE OF THE RE-ROUTE: the board is now INSIDE the exact-null window. Low end of the residual band (18.5 nH) minus the window's low edge (16.041 nH) = +2.459 nH. The pre-re-route board read -7.069 nH here (7.21 nH against a 14.279 nH edge). A negative reading means the re-route has been undone and the README's two-sided-null language must be retracted.
(C) central residual 19.5 nH is +3.459 nH inside the window.
(C) top of the residual band 23.3 nH is +7.259 nH inside.

(C) THE ONE PLACE THE BOARD STILL FALLS OUT, and it is asserted as a MAX so it cannot be quietly dropped: at the 6.5 pF end of the parasitic band the window starts at 18.816 nH, so an 18.5 nH build is -0.316 nH short and C1 bottoms out. See s11_corners.cir block D for what that costs: under 0.07 dB.

(C) at the +5% resistance corner with the nominal parasitic the window starts at 17.689 nH and an 18.5 nH build clears it by +0.811 nH - two-sided, but this is the tightest R x L combination at the nominal parasitic.
(C) crit. 2 across the residual band at nominal R and parasitic: L = 18.5 nH -> 55.462 dB.
(C) crit. 2 across the residual band at nominal R and parasitic: L = 19.5 nH -> 54.550 dB.
(C) crit. 2 across the residual band at nominal R and parasitic: L = 23.3 nH -> 51.464 dB.
(D) L = 1 pH, i.e. NO residual at all, trimmer at its stop: 32.00 dB. Spec is met with the residual completely absent - the 5.4 pF port alone never breaks 26 dB.
(D) L = 30 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 47.088 dB.
(D) L = 60 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 35.162 dB.
(D) L = 90 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 28.305 dB.
(D) L = 96.661 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 27.116 dB.
(D) L = 100 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 26.520 dB.
(D) L = 102 nH at R = 50, best clamped setting: 26.147 dB. Tight bracket - warning severity by design.

(D) L = 103 nH: 25.959 dB - below spec. With rl_dl102 this brackets the README NUMBER: at R = 50 with the delivered 1-30 pF trimmer and the 5.4 pF port, RL >= 26 dB holds out to L = 102-103 nH (closed-form crossing 102.78 nH, X = 16.15 ohm).
(D) L = 110 nH: 24.64 dB. Past spec authority, and no trimmer setting recovers it.
(D) the same authority question at R = 52.5, where the resistance transformation bites long before the trimmer runs out of range: L = 70 nH gives 26.78 dB.

(D) L = 76.859 nH at R = 52.5: 26.000 dB. The +5% corner's spec authority ends at 76.86 nH - a quarter of the nominal-resistance figure - and it is set by Reff = R + X^2/R, not by the trimmer. reff_limit.cir derives the same 76.86 nH from closed form with an IDEAL unlimited tuner and gets the same answer, which is the proof that the part is not the limit there. UNCHANGED by the re-route, as it must be.
(D) L = 80 nH at R = 52.5: 25.65 dB - fails, and no setting of C1 recovers it. The board's 23.3 nH worst residual uses 30% of that authority.

(E) WAS THE RE-ROUTE WORTH IT, like for like: at the binding R = 52.5 corner with each board at its own CENTRAL estimate, 31.190 dB (7.21 nH, 4.7 pF, C1 hard against its 1 pF stop) -> 31.671 dB (19.5 nH, 5.4 pF, C1 at a real null) = +0.481 dB. The re-route bought margin AND the two-sided null; it did not trade one for the other.

(E) the same question WORST-BUILD to WORST-BUILD, which is the number that belongs in the README: the old board's worst credible build (R 52.5 / 7.21 nH / 6.0 pF, C1 bottomed) read 30.375 dB; the new board's worst of 48 (R 52.5 / 23.3 nH, C1 at a true null) reads 31.433 dB = +1.059 dB. Note the two deltas differ (0.48 vs 1.06) because the worst corner MOVED: it used to be set by the pessimistic parasitic and is now set by the top of the residual band. Quoting either one as 'the' improvement without saying which comparison it is would be misleading.
(E) the old board's worst credible build, kept live: 30.375 dB. Reproduces the retired bench's rl_r525_p60_fc.
(E) the new board's worst of 48: 31.433 dB. Cross-checks s11_band.cir rl_r525_p47_l233_fc to 4 decimals.
(E) the BEFORE instance, kept in the bench so the comparison cannot drift: 31.190 dB. This reproduces the retired bench's rl_r525_p47_fc to 4 decimals.
(E) and the BEFORE trimmer setting, computed and clamped by the same ctset(): exactly 1.000 pF, i.e. bottomed out. This is the defect the re-route removed, kept live as a reference.
(E) the AFTER setting at the same corner: 1.6508 pF, off the stop.

(E) THE FREE LUNCH IS OVER, and this is the bound that says so. Before the re-route, adding inductance IMPROVED the binding corner (+0.72 dB for the first 7 nH) because the fixed port capacitance was over-correcting a 7.21 nH residual. From 19.5 nH the null is interior, so further inductance only buys Reff: going on to 30 nH costs -0.737 dB. Asserted as a MAX of 0 - a positive reading means the board has fallen back below its null window and the re-route has been undone.
(E) and 40 nH costs -1.636 dB. The board is now on the correct side of the optimum: 19.5 nH is 3.46 nH past the window's low edge and every further nH is spent, not earned.
(E) crit. 2 still holds at 30 nH / R = 52.5: 30.93 dB - the residual would have to more than triple before the re-route became a spec problem.
